newsitem.title: ECUADOR: New Ecuador president known as tough negotiator.
newsitem.headline: New Ecuador president known as tough negotiator.

text.p: Fabian Alarcon, sworn in as Ecuador's new president after Congress voted to oust Abdala Bucaram, is a politician know for sharp negotiating skills.
"I accept the responsibility and will abide by my duties even with my own life," said Alarcon after being handed the country's top job on Thursday.
The 50-year-old head of Congress was not long ago a staunch ally of Bucaram. He was even considered early last year as Bucaram's possible running mate for last July's general elections.
Alarcon accompanied Bucaram during the campaign, standing firmly by his side while Bucaram insulted his political adversaries or belted out pop tunes by local group Los Iracundos.
Alarcon twice held the post of Congress president and was vice-president in charge in 1995 when then vice-president Alberto Dahik fled the country after being accused of corruption.
Bucaram supporters accused Alarcon of being a spineless politician who reneged of his former ally to grab the presidency.
"Who is not loyal to a friend will not be loyal to the country," said lawmaker Marco Proano.
